chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya raised it from Aban who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A young girl from us had an ulcer in her private part, and the blood was flowing. She did not know whether it was from the blood of menstruation or from the blood of the ulcer.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Instruct her to lie down on her back, then raise her two legs, then insert her middle finger. If the blood comes out from the right side, it is from menstruation, and if it comes out from the left side, it is from the ulcer.'
ai.seo_question: How to distinguish between menstrual blood and bleeding from an ulcer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a specific physical diagnostic method (istikhraj) used by Shia jurists to distinguish between menstrual blood and non-menstrual bleeding (damm al-faq') from ulcers or wounds. By inserting the middle finger to observe the exit point of the blood, the Imam (peace be upon him) provides a practical criterion for determining ritual purity status, which remains a key reference in fiqh al-‘ila (jurisprudence of women's health).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it from Aban who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A young girl from us had an ulcer in her private part, and the blood flowed. She did not know whether it is from the blood of the ulcer’. So heasws said: ‘Instruct her, so let her lie down upon her back, then raise her two legs, then insert her middle finger. So it the blood comes out from the right hand side, so it is from the menstruation (Haydh), but if it comes out from the left hand side, so it is from the ulcer’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya in a marfu‘ manner has narrated from Aban who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a young woman of our people has a wound in her vagina. She finds bleeding but does not know if it is because of Hayd (menses) or because of the wound and blood flows. He (the Imam) said, ‘Instruct her to lie down on her back, raise her legs and place her middle finger inside. If blood comes from the right side, it is because of Hayd (menses); if it comes from the left side, it is because of the wound.’”
